rfm_tuples.R: Management/board confidence in the relacorilant hypercortisolism NDA — relacorilant was the single most-discussed pipeline asset across the 10-K Item 1/MD&A, with the December 2024 NDA submission framed as the catalyst for franchise expansion beyond Korlym/Teva-generic erosion.
rfm_tuples.f: Parse Form 4 XML for ALL non-derivative S/P transactions by named officers in the 4 months preceding the Dec 30, 2025 CRL (Sept-Dec 2025), measure dollar magnitude and clustering vs trailing baseline.
rfm_tuples.M_value: In the 4 months before the Dec 30, 2025 CRL, named officers executed at least 35 open-market sale transactions totalling well over $20M at peak prices ($70-90/sh). CEO Joseph Belanoff: ~110,000 sh sold Sept-Nov 2025 for ~$8.2M @ avg ~$75. CDO William Guyer: ~60,000 sh sold for ~$4.7M @ avg ~$78. President of Endocrinology Sean Maduck: ~60,000 sh sold for ~$4.6M @ avg ~$77. CAO/CTO Joseph Lyon: ~15,000 sh sold for ~$1.1M. Most-recent sales (Oct 7 Guyer @$89.94; Nov 5 Belanoff/Guyer @$74-76) occurred 8 weeks before the CRL. All identified sales executed under pre-existing Rule 10b5-1 plans (`<aff10b5One>true</aff10b5One>` flag present in XML). 12-mo aggregate officer SALES: ~$104.7M across 129 transactions. 12-mo open-market officer PURCHASES: $0.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Even adjusting for 10b5-1 plans, the dollar magnitude and tight clustering at LOCAL HIGH prices (CORT ran from ~$30 in mid-2023 to ~$90 in Oct 2025) constitutes a quintessential 'cash out the top' tape by the entire C-suite — Belanoff, Maduck, Guyer, Lyon, Robb, Mokari, Hunt all selling, none buying. The asymmetry is total: P:S ratio is essentially 0 for officers. Under the honesty-alpha framework, this is the cleanest insider-sell signal in the forward-test universe.

rfm_tuples.R: Implicit Mode-B claim: pre-existing 10b5-1 plans mean officer sales are scheduled and uncorrelated with non-public clinical/regulatory information.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference 10b5-1 plan ADOPTION dates (disclosed in 10-K Item 9B and 10-Q Item 5) against the relacorilant FDA review timeline and Dec 30, 2025 CRL.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K Item 9B discloses Sean Maduck (President, Corcept Endocrinology) adopted a 10b5-1 plan on 2025-12-08 covering up to 600,000 shares (~$50M+ at then-prevailing prices), expiring 2027-06-30. CFO Atabak Mokari adopted a 10b5-1 plan on 2025-12-12 covering up to 200,000 shares, expiring 2027-03-14. Both plans were adopted in the FINAL 22-18 DAYS BEFORE the Dec 30, 2025 FDA CRL. PDUFA cycle for endogenous-hypercortisolism NDA filed Dec 2024 = approximately 10-month standard review (PDUFA target ~Oct/Nov 2025, extended). FDA late-cycle communications, including the issuance of post-action letters and labeling-discussion meetings, would routinely occur 30-60 days before action — placing knowledge of CRL likelihood squarely within the adoption window for these plans. The 10-Q for Q1 2025 (May 2025), Q2 2025 (Jul 2025), and Q3 2025 (Nov 2025) ALL disclosed NO new plan adoptions — i.e., the company-wide pattern of fresh plan adoptions in early December 2025, weeks before a known-pending FDA decision, is anomalous and not a routine annual cycle.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the strongest Mode-B forensic finding. Two senior executives — President of the hypercortisolism franchise (the asset most directly tied to the CRL outcome) and the CFO — adopted large new 10b5-1 plans in the 2-3 weeks immediately preceding a CRL that was likely already foreshadowed by late-cycle FDA communications. The 800,000-share aggregate authorization at ~$80/sh = ~$64M of pre-authorized selling. Plans signed under a known-pending negative catalyst, even if technically compliant with cooling-off periods, are precisely the structural setup that the SEC's 2022 amendments to Rule 10b5-1 were designed to surface as a red flag. Combined with the Q4 2025 sales tape, this directly contradicts the issuer's implied confidence in the relacorilant approval narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied: after a major negative catalyst (CRL), aligned management should not continue selling at depressed prices unless trading is rigidly mechanical.
rfm_tuples.f: Form 4 review of officer sales POST Dec 30, 2025 CRL through cutoff.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Officer sales CONTINUED after the CRL even at prices ~50% below the September peak: CDO Guyer sold 20,000 sh @ $35.18 on 2026-01-06 (7 days after CRL); CEO Belanoff sold 26,198 sh @ $50.07 on 2026-03-25 ($1.3M); CEO Belanoff sold 40,000 sh @ $50.10 on 2026-05-01 ($2.0M); Guyer sold another 60,000 sh between Feb-May 2026 for ~$3M. Post-CRL aggregate officer sales: ~$7.4M. Director G. Leonard Baker (Sutter Hill Ventures) BOUGHT 100,000 sh open-market on 2026-03-17 for $3.31M at avg $33.13 (the only material insider PURCHASE in 18 months). Director James Wilson ADOPTED a new 10b5-1 plan on 2026-03-12 to sell up to 100,000 sh through 2027-03-15.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mixed but tilted negative. Baker's $3.3M buy at $33 is a meaningful directional vote and the lone bright spot — Sutter Hill is a long-time deep-information holder. However, the C-suite did NOT use the post-CRL window to signal personal conviction via open-market purchases; instead they continued executing scheduled sales (CEO Belanoff specifically continued through May 2026). And board-member Wilson adopted a fresh sell-plan in the SAME WEEK Baker was buying — i.e., the board itself is internally split with one director buying and another setting up to sell. Net: insider tape is asymmetrically negative.

rfm_tuples.R: "On December 30, 2025, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter ('CRL') declining to approve relacorilant. While the letter acknowledged that our GRACE trial had met its primary endpoint and that our GRADIENT trial had provided confirmatory evidence, the FDA stated that additional evidence of efficacy would be required for approval. We are working with the FDA to determine relacorilant's optimal path to approval."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: verify CRL existence and characterize what 'additional evidence of efficacy' likely entails. Mode-B: assess whether the issuer is downplaying the magnitude (a 'we are working with FDA' framing on a pivotal-asset CRL is a known soft-pedal pattern).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + clinical_trials (Mode B via GRACE/GRADIENT trial design)
rfm_tuples.M_value: GRADIENT's primary endpoint was the relacorilant-vs-placebo systolic-blood-pressure delta — and the 10-K admits 'The comparison between those who received relacorilant and placebo was NOT statistically significant.' Issuer characterizes GRADIENT as 'confirmatory' but the primary endpoint MISSED stat-sig. GRACE used an unusual randomized-withdrawal design (only patients who responded in open-label phase were randomized to withdrawal), which can inflate apparent efficacy by enriching for responders. The CRL specifically cited 'additional evidence of efficacy' — strongly implying FDA viewed the open-label/withdrawal GRACE design and the non-significant GRADIENT primary as insufficient. The most-likely remedy is another Phase 3 placebo-controlled trial = 24-48 months delay minimum, materially deferring hypercortisolism revenue beyond Korlym/Teva-generic erosion timeline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: the issuer language is honest in the strict sense (it discloses GRADIENT's primary endpoint missed) but frames the CRL as a procedural step ('working with the FDA') rather than what it likely is — a multi-year derailment of the cornerstone pipeline asset. The asymmetry between management's confidence framing (continued spend, continued sales-force buildout) and the FDA's substantive critique is large.

rfm_tuples.R: "In March 2026, the FDA approved Lifyorli™ (relacorilant) in combination with nab-paclitaxel...In April 2026, we began selling and distributing Lifyorli in the United States." Management positions Lifyorli as the franchise-expanding ovarian-cancer launch.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify Q1 2026 P&L impact of Lifyorli pre-launch spend and post-CRL spend rebalancing; check cash burn and operating-loss trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 net LOSS of $31.8M vs Q1 2025 net INCOME of $20.5M — a $52M YoY swing despite revenue UP only 4.9% ($164.9M vs $157.2M). SG&A exploded +60% YoY to $145.4M (vs $90.7M) — driven by Lifyorli launch buildout and hypercortisolism commercialization. R&D up 9% to $66.3M. Operating loss $49.6M vs operating income $3.4M prior year. Cash + marketable securities declined from $532.4M (Dec 31, 2025) to $515.4M (Mar 31, 2026); operating cash flow Q1 2026 = ($16.8M) USED vs ($4.8M) PROVIDED prior year. The Stock Repurchase Program ($172.9M in FY25 at avg $66.71) appears HALTED in Q1 2026 — only $5.8M of share repurchases, all related to net-settlement of option exercises, no open-market repurchases under the program.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Cash position is intact but the burn trajectory is sharp — Q1 2026 burn rate annualizes to ~$67M operating loss with SG&A still ramping. Lifyorli ovarian-cancer launch will require sustained heavy spend against established oncology competitors (PARP-inhibitor combos), and the addressable population (platinum-resistant ovarian, post-bevacizumab) is small. The fact that the company HALTED open-market buybacks (FY25 ran $172.9M @ $66.71; Q1 2026 ZERO open-market) at the moment the stock is most discounted is another negative-conviction signal — exactly the opposite of management putting capital to work at perceived value.

rfm_tuples.R: "Net product revenue was $761.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025...The increase...was driven by a 37.0 percent increase in sales volume, partially offset by a 17.7 percent decrease in average price due to higher sales volume from our authorized generic version of Korlym." Implied claim: business is healthy with volume growing.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the Teva generic litigation outcome and quantify the structural pricing exposure of the Korlym franchise.
rfm_tuples.M_value: On 2026-02-19 the Federal Circuit AFFIRMED the District Court's December 2023 ruling that Teva's generic Korlym does NOT infringe the '214 or '800 method-of-use patents. Teva's generic has been on the market since January 2024. CORT launched its own authorized generic in June 2024 as a defensive move. The Q1 2026 10-Q discloses a petition for rehearing filed April 22, 2026 — long-shot procedural step. Meanwhile, Sun Pharmaceutical and Hikma have litigation settlements allowing them to enter with their own generics 'provided FDA has approved their products and Teva's generic product remains commercially available' — i.e., a multi-generic Korlym market is a question of when, not if. The 17.7% YoY price decline is the leading edge of a structural erosion that will deepen as additional generics enter. The '36% volume +' framing masks the price normalization toward generic levels.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honestly disclosed — issuer transparent about the patent loss and the multi-generic future. But the combination of (a) CRL on relacorilant-Cushing's (the patent-protected replacement franchise), (b) Federal Circuit affirmance of Teva non-infringement, and (c) standby Sun/Hikma generics is a classic franchise-cliff setup. The price compression already evident in 2025 (-17.7%) will worsen.

rfm_tuples.R: "In June 2025, we notified Optime that it would cease to be our exclusive specialty pharmacy and in October 2025, we delivered a notice of termination of our agreement with them, effective January 8, 2026. In the fourth quarter of 2025, substantially all of our specialty pharmacy services were transferred from Optime to Curant Health Georgia, LLC ('Curant')."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given Teva has a separate ANTITRUST lawsuit pending (N.D. Cal. 5:24-cv-03567) accusing CORT and Optime of anticompetitive conduct, assess whether the abrupt Optime termination is defensive litigation positioning vs neutral operational change.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Teva Antitrust Litigation filed 2024-06-13, alleges CORT-Optime conspired to suppress generic Korlym distribution. On 2025-09-12 the District Court granted-in-part the motion to dismiss but Teva refiled (SAC, then TAC adding claims regarding the NEW Curant relationship). Trial now scheduled for March 2027. Curant agreement effective June 2025 — i.e., CORT was lining up a NEW specialty-pharmacy vendor in the same window it was being sued for anticompetitive use of the OLD vendor. Aetna parallel litigation also pending in CA state court (substantially similar allegations). The Q1 2025 10-Q discloses a hearing on motions to dismiss took place 2026-02-18 — no clean dismissal of the antitrust claims is currently in hand.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: the Optime-to-Curant transition is framed by management as a normal vendor change but the timing (during active antitrust litigation accusing CORT-Optime of exactly this exclusive-distribution conduct) and the fact that Teva's TAC NOW INCLUDES CURANT-specific claims suggests this is contested. The litigation overhang is material — antitrust trebled damages on Korlym revenue would be a multi-year top-line and balance-sheet risk.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Eligible label: 1-3 prior systemic regimens, at least one of which included bevacizumab. Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer incidence in the US ~13,000-15,000/yr. Bevacizumab-pretreated subset is a fraction. Drug pricing for oncology orphan combos with nab-paclitaxel typically $100-200K/patient/yr course. Even on optimistic 30% market share over 24 months = ~$200-400M annualized peak. Lifyorli does NOT meaningfully replace the hypercortisolism CRL — different patient, different prescriber (oncologists), different sales-force build. Q1 2026 SG&A already burning at $145M/qtr ($580M annualized) and revenue still at $660M annualized — Lifyorli launch economics are unclear and the company has never sold an oncology drug.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Without analyst-model access or 2026 revenue guidance breakout, the precise Lifyorli contribution is unverifiable from the filing itself. Issuer does not provide explicit Lifyorli revenue guidance in either the 10-K (filed Feb 24, 2026, before approval) or the Q1 2026 10-Q (one month post-launch). Mode-B gap: this is the bull case management is now selling, but with no guidance and no precedent oncology launch, sizing the contribution requires assumptions outside the filing.

summary: CORT is the inverse of the ABG setup. Despite a -33% drawdown and intact $515M cash position, the forensic tape is unambiguously NEGATIVE: ~$105M of 12-month officer open-market sales vs ZERO officer open-market purchases; the entire C-suite (CEO Belanoff, President Maduck, CFO Mokari, CDO Guyer, CAO/CTO Lyon, CBO Robb, CSO Hunt) sold into the September-October 2025 price peak ($70-90). The strongest Mode-B finding: President of the hypercortisolism franchise (Maduck) and CFO (Mokari) adopted FRESH 10b5-1 plans on Dec 8 and Dec 12, 2025 — 18-22 days BEFORE the Dec 30, 2025 FDA CRL — covering aggregate 800,000 shares (~$64M). Late-cycle FDA communications would routinely flag CRL likelihood within that adoption window. No new plans adopted in Q1/Q2/Q3 2025; the Q4 2025 plan adoption cluster is anomalous. Post-CRL officer selling continued ($7.4M Jan-May 2026); only meaningful buy was a single director (G. Leonard Baker, Sutter Hill) at $33 = $3.3M. Stock Repurchase Program executed at $66.71 avg in FY25 then HALTED at the post-CRL discount — same wrong-way conviction as the insider tape. Business is honestly disclosed (CRL acknowledged, GRADIENT primary endpoint miss admitted, Teva non-infringement loss disclosed) but the cornerstone franchise-expansion asset is derailed (likely 24-48 months for additional Phase 3), Korlym pricing erodes -17.7% YoY against multiple incoming generics, Q1 2026 swung to net loss with SG&A +60% YoY, and Lifyorli oncology launch is a small-population orphan with no precedent for CORT in oncology selling. Verdict: SHORT-tier. Severity: 1 PASS / 1 UNVERIFIABLE / 5 MODERATE / 2 SEVERE / 1 RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE.
